### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.tabline

### Question

Is it possible to customize the tabline as shown in the screenshot, where I have the tab number (e.g., "01", "02", "03") on the left and the file name (e.g., "Blink.lua") on the right?
![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/629f3d7f-cb98-4659-a90c-14ac689e4432)

The screenshot shows how the  [tabby](https://github.com/nanozuki/tabby.nvim) plugin does it, but I was wondering if something similar can be achieved with `mini.tabline`.

Thank you!

comment_data.body:
I’ve managed to achieve this with tabs, 
![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f423e222-cf3e-464c-9d69-77a998ac2cb8)


but I haven’t been able to hide the file names when switching tabs. Also, I still need to add a Nixos icon to the left of the tabs, but I'm not sure how to do that

code:
```lua
vim.o.tabline = "%!v:lua.MyTabLine() .. v:lua.MiniTabline.make_tabline_string()"

function _G.MyTabLine()
    local tabline = ""
    for i = 1, vim.fn.tabpagenr("$") do
        local is_tab = vim.fn.tabpagenr() == i
        tabline = tabline
            .. (is_tab and "%#MiniTablineTabpagesection#" or "%#Normal#")
            .. " "
            .. "%"
            .. (is_tab and "  " or "  ")
            .. i
            .. " "
    end
    return tabline
end

comment_data.body: 'mini.tabline' is not designed for this kind of customization, I am afraid. The closest you can do to showing only single "tab" (if I understand correctly what you mean here) is try finding the [`config.format`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4446e834c30c799627d65691c73d59638e5c965f/doc/mini-tabline.txt#L94-L96) that works best for you. For example, returning empty string for non-current buffers.

@echasnovski I managed to hide non-current buffers by customizing the `config.format`, but I encountered an issue: when I switch to another tab and open a buffer, it doesn't display the file name properly. Any suggestions on how to handle this scenario?

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a36b8193-3dc8-4434-a504-409f4dd90f0a

here code:
```lua 
MiniTabline.setup({
    set_vim_settings = true,
    format = function(buf_id, label)
        local suffix = vim.bo[buf_id].modified and "  " or "  "
        for i = 1, vim.fn.tabpagenr("$") do
            local is_tab = vim.fn.tabpagenr() == i
            local v, _ = MiniTabline.default_format(buf_id, label)
            if is_tab then
                return suffix .. v
            else
                return ""
            end
        end
        -- stylua: ignore
        -- return suffix .. v
    end,
    show_icons = true,
    tabpage_section = "right",
})

function _G.MyTabLine()
    local tabline = ""
    local os_icon, hl = MiniIcons.get("os", "nixos")
    for i = 1, vim.fn.tabpagenr("$") do
        local is_tab = vim.fn.tabpagenr() == i
        tabline = tabline
            .. (is_tab and "%#MiniTablineTabpagesection#" or "%#Normal#")
            .. " "
            .. "%"
            .. (is_tab and "  " or "  ")
            .. i
            .. " "
    end
    return "%#" .. hl .. "# " .. os_icon .. " " .. tabline --  .. .. "%=%"
end

reply_data.body: Tabpage is not the same as buffer (see `:h windows-intro`). In `config.format` you cycle through tabpages, not buffers. To return empty string for non-current buffers it should start with something like `if buf_id ~= vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() then return '' end`.

@echasnovski thanks so much, this worked for me with `if buf_id ~= vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() then return '' end` :)  
Also, another way that worked for me is this code:

```lua
format = function(buf_id, label)
        local current_tab = vim.fn.tabpagenr()
        local tab_buffers = vim.fn.tabpagebuflist(current_tab)
        if vim.tbl_contains(tab_buffers, buf_id) then
            local v, _ = MiniTabline.default_format(buf_id, label)
            local suffix = vim.bo[buf_id].modified and "  " or "  "
            return suffix .. v
        end
        return ""
    end,
```

reply_data.body:
> Also, another way that worked for me is this code:

Beware that this will call `tabpagenr()`, `tabpagebuflist()`, and `vim.tbl_contains()` (which is somewhat expensive as it does linear search) on *every* currently listed buffer. This is basically `O(n*m)` complexity with `n` - number of all listed buffers and `m` - number of buffers visible in current tabpage, compared to essentially `O(n)` with `vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()` approach which is essentially `O(1)` because `nvim_get_current_buf()` is really fast.

> Sorry, one more question: is it possible to color the icon of the file? If not, that’s fine. Thanks again! :)
